newsitem.title: JAPAN: ALL TOKYO CORN FUTURES FALL SHARPLY ON STRONG YEN.
newsitem.headline: ALL TOKYO CORN FUTURES FALL SHARPLY ON STRONG YEN.

text.p: Tokyo corn futures ended sharply lower on Monday, as the yen's strong rally against the dollar triggered heavy selling by local investors, traders said.

All contracts plunged by their 400 yen daily limits by the close, with the benchmark July 1998 down 400 yen at 13,630 yen per tonne. Limit-less spot September 1997 contract was down 480 yen at 14,520 yen.
The yen's steep gains against the dollar during the weekend triggered selling from local investors, traders said. The weaker CBOT overnight corn trading also accelerated the bearish mood, they said.

Traders said they're watching the USDA crop reports, which is to be released on Tuesday. "But local investors will be sidelined basically this week, because of the Japanese holidays," a brokerage house trader said.

The spot September corn contract on the CBOT Project A trading system was trading at $2.48 per bushel at 0710 GMT, against $2.53-1/2 at Friday's close. Spot August CBOT soybean futures were at $7.24 per bushel at 0710 GMT, against $7.39-3/4 at Friday's close.
